newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: S&P Marketscope sees Smart car risk to SMH.
newsitem.headline: S&P Marketscope sees Smart car risk to SMH.

text.p: Standard & Poor's Marketscope said it saw greater risks than generally recognised to Swiss watchmaker SMH from its Smart Car joint venture with Daimler-Benz AG unit Mercedes-Benz AG.
Marketscope's Equity Research report concluded the risks were not reflected in the share price of Suisse Microelectronique et d'Horologerie (SMH), home of major watch brands including Swatch.
SMH bearers fell 2.9 two percent or 25 Swiss francs to close at 822 francs on news of the study, traders said.

"Although we recognise the subjectivity of forecasting Smart sales, we have found that the automotive industry is sceptical and we conclude that the risks are not reflected in the SMH share price," the report said.
It said the project's forecasted annual sales of 200,000 units by the year 2000 "may prove wildly optimistic".

Its findings were based on an analysis of car markets and market share among small vehicles that will be competition for Micro Compact Car (MCC), the name of the joint venture. The Smart Car is due to be launched in early 1998.
"We think it extremely unlikely that MCC will be profitable and predict large losses in 1998," the study said.
"The risks are much greater than generally appreciated," it added.
SMH has a 49 percent stake in MCC capital, with the remaining 51 percent held by Mercedes.
Marketscope said it believed the main engine of growth at SMH would remain the watch business.

"We are not assuming a significant profit contribution from the telecommunications joint venture over the near term because the relationship with Siemens is still far from clear and the product line unconvincing," it added about SMH's other major venture out of watchmaking.
